sourceBinding.checks: Compared every packet sourceEnglish paragraph to the canonical lesson body and registry body sourceEnglish; compared every currentSesothoDraft paragraph to the registry sesothoDraft. All 20 pairs matched exactly and in order. No repository files changed.

overall: Meaning is mostly bounded and the critical geometry, dimensions, crop identities, wet-clay prohibition, and deeper-cultivation conditions are held in English. Request the repairs/holds below before wiring. This is a semantic backcheck, not fluency approval.

findings.note: Candidate preserves the registry text exactly. Its 'Metso e hola butle' reads as roots grow slowly rather than explicitly 'roots slow down'; this is an existing localized sentence, so do not treat the candidate as a correction of it.
'Tshireletso e bonolo' conveys the simple protection framing. Both-side reachability and permanent paths remain exact English, preserving the access geometry.
Exact width range, reach from either path, and never-touching the growing area remain English. 'Ke yona working number' conveys that this is the working number; no geometry or numeric change.
Preserved text retains the question about reaching the middle without stepping inside and the try-before-planting instruction.
Preserved text retains that no one bed shape suits every place.
The complete least-disturbance and solves-your-problem condition stays exact English; only 'Qala ka' supplies the ordinary start framing.
'Boholo ba' retains most-scope. No-dig and build-fertility-on-top remain explicit. 'Structure' is retained as a technical term, with 'Tlohela ... e le jwalo' preserving leave it as it is.
Wet-clay prohibition and the severe compaction/poor drainage trigger, identify-the-cause step, local advice, and before-deeper-cultivation order are all preserved verbatim.
Raised beds are said to suit wet ground; the drainage-away condition remains exact English. No claim that raised beds solve drainage is added.
Sunken beds are said to suit dry ground; the desire to catch and hold the rain received remains exact English. No universal suitability claim is added.
Preserved text retains observation after heavy rain, sitting/runoff, and combining that observation with soil/drainage advice before bed choice.
The translated introduction conveys that some crops do not like root disturbance. The direct-sowing comparison and the exact crop list Beans, carrots and maize remain English.

findings.candidateIssue: 'Tomatoes le brassicas di wela moo' can read literally as tomatoes and brassicas falling there; it does not reliably express that these crops belong in the nursery-start group.
findings.recommendedCandidate: Others do better with a protected start in a nursery, then transplanting. Tomatoes and brassicas belong there.
findings.note: Keep the crop names and group-membership sentence in English unless a checked Sesotho wording is available. The protected nursery start and transplanting sequence already remain exact.
Spacing guidance for crop, variety and local conditions, plus packet/local-grower advice, remain exact English. The translated ending retains observing crowding as plants grow/develop.

findings.candidateIssue: 'Tshwaya bed' means mark the bed, but does not clearly retain 'mark the bed out' as laying out its boundaries before planting.
findings.recommendedCandidate: Pele o lema, mark the bed out.
findings.note: Keep the timing in Sesotho and hold the layout action in English until 'mark out' is verified. Paragraph 16's rectangle marking does not remove the need to preserve this exact action.
Width 1.2 metres, length 3 metres, and one practice bed remain in source order. No number or unit changed.
Pegs and string remain named; the rectangle is marked and both access paths are explicitly preserved. No alternate geometry is introduced.

findings.candidateIssue: 'Ebe o lokisa mobu wa hao' reads as 'then prepare your soil'; source says 'prepare for your own soil', emphasizing adaptation to the grower's soil rather than merely preparing soil.
findings.recommendedCandidate: Then prepare for your own soil — no-dig first, and dig deeper only if your ground genuinely needs it.
findings.note: Hold the complete introductory clause in English. The no-dig-first order and dig-deeper-only-if-genuinely-needed condition are already retained exactly and must remain so.

Both once-existing conditions and their order are retained: keep paths once present; protect the growing area once present. 'Mohala wa thapo' is recognizable as a string/rope line, and the idea-to-decision relation is preserved.
The easier-to-improve result, every-season timing, and causal explanation that people stopped stepping/walking on the bed are retained.

protectionAudit.bothSidesReachability: Exact English retained in paragraphs 1 and 2.
protectionAudit.dimensionsAndNoFootTraffic: Exact source range and never-touch/growing-area condition retained in paragraph 2; 1.2m by 3m practice bed retained in paragraph 15.
protectionAudit.wetClayAndDeeperCultivation: Exact English prohibition and severe-condition/local-advice-before-deeper-cultivation sequence retained in paragraph 7; paragraph 17 retains no-dig-first and deeper only when genuinely needed.
protectionAudit.cropIdentityAndEstablishment: Beans, carrots, maize, tomatoes and brassicas unchanged; direct sow and protected nursery start/transplanting held in English. Paragraph 12 group-membership framing needs hold.
protectionAudit.soilAndBedConditions: Wet-ground drainage-away and dry-ground rain-catching conditions held in English in paragraphs 8 and 9; no new bed prescription.
